mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% for two consecutive months signals central bank over-tightening, which raises real discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (p > 0.1), or CPIAUCSL does not sustain a two-month rise above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected discount rate increases, reducing the present value of future earnings for equities and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during such FEDFUNDS jumps.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2,000 monthly for three consecutive months coincides with corporate hiring acceleration, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 for ≥3 consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market strengthening in expansion phase
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during such labor strength episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods demand) show double-digit monthly growth in the same quarter, it signals robust economic momentum that supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both grow by ≥10% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the double-digit growth in both proxies (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5 points in a month, followed by a sustained drop over the next two months, reflects supply-side weakness that reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5 points in month 1 and <100 in month 2
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during such INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates labor market tightening and reduces the risk of wage growth shocks, which tends to support equity valuations and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite UNRATE falling below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (indicated by a 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 1.00%), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 60-day forward returns as lower real rates encourage risk-on sentiment and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) during the easing regime.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (industrial production) by at least 5% in the same month creates cross-channel demand momentum that elevates earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both increase by ≥5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during such dual-proxy strength.
